persona.bio: Cashier at a big box store. Register and stocking shelves, sometimes self checkout. Mostly ringing people up and dealing with returns and coupons that don't scan. When it's slow she faces shelves and does go backs. She swaps shifts with coworkers by text. Few words, not much of a writer. She has never used AI, and the store's handbook says no AI tools at work.

steps.firstStep: I’m a cashier at a big box store and I answer customer messages all day by text. Write a short, polite reply in plain language that a cashier can send. Keep it under 60 words, friendly and clear, and do not invent store policies. Here is what the customer asked: [paste the customer’s message here]

steps.note: I work as a cashier at a big box store. I scan items, handle returns, count the till, and answer price and coupon questions. The people I write to are customers, and sometimes coworkers. I like short, friendly, plain replies that sound like a real person. Two or three sentences is plenty. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, dates, store rules or return policies. Use square brackets for anything I need to fill in. Never write anything about someone’s private information. Keep the draft simple so I can read it, change it and send it myself.

steps.title: Your customer texts, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your customer replies live on your phone’s keyboard, each one a few letters away. You stop typing the same answer from scratch many times a day. Each reply fits after you change a name or a time, so you read it, adjust it and send it.

material.label: Your replies
items: Hi [first name], thanks for reaching out. I can check on that for you. Can you tell me the item and what you need?
Hi [first name], for a return without a receipt, store credit may be an option. Please check with a manager on [what applies] and we will go from there.
Hi [first name], I am not able to confirm that price by text. Please bring the item to a register or a price check scanner and we will look it up with you.
Hi [first name], if a coupon does not scan, bring it to the front and I will ask a manager to check it. It depends on [coupon details].
Thanks for waiting, [first name]. I checked and [answer]. Let me know if you need anything else.
Hi [first name], I am sorry about the trouble. A manager can help with this best. Please ask for them when you come in on [day and time].
Hi [first name], I am not able to help with that one. Please ask a manager or call the store at [store phone number].
Thanks, [first name]. Have a good day.

safeUse: Never type a customer’s name, phone number, address, or card or payment details into a chat tool.
Never type receipt numbers, loyalty account numbers or anything from a customer’s order.
Never type your store’s till counts, safe details or employee numbers.
Check what your store allows before using any AI tool for work.
Read every reply before you send it, and check prices, coupon and return rules against what your manager gives you.
steps.askMessage: Hi [manager or IT contact], I would like to know which AI tools, if any, are approved for my work as a cashier, and what I may use them for. I have two uses in mind. One is drafting replies to customer messages. The other is working out how to handle returns and coupons that do not scan. I would not enter any customer details, and I would read everything before using it. Both of these wait for the company’s OK, so please let me know what is allowed.

design.today: You answer messages many times a day, each one from scratch.
design.newWay: Your company restricts AI, so AI does not touch this task at all. Instead you keep a short set of your own saved replies for the questions you get most, each a few letters away on your phone. You read each one, change what needs changing, and send it yourself. You stop retyping the same answer, and every reply still sounds like you and follows store policy.

steps.goal: Pick the ten messages you answer most often, without writing down any customer's name or private details.
Write one short answer to each in your own words, and check each against your store's policy or ask a manager where you are unsure.
Save each answer so it is a few letters away when you type.
Look over the saved answers every so often and update any that no longer match store policy.
